officialTitle: Neratinib after trastuzumab-based adjuvant therapy in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer (ExteNET): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Between July 9, 2009, and Oct 24, 2011, we randomly assigned 2840 women to receive neratinib (n=1420) or placebo (n=1420).
design.notes: Stratified by hormone receptor status, nodal status and trastuzumab regimen. Inclusion amended in 2010 to stage 2-3 disease within 1 year of trastuzumab completion. No mandatory diarrhoea prophylaxis.

clinicalQuestion: Does 1 year of neratinib after completion of trastuzumab-based adjuvant therapy improve invasive disease-free survival in HER2-positive early breast cancer?

pico.population: Women with stage 1-3 (later 2-3) HER2-positive breast cancer who had completed neoadjuvant/adjuvant trastuzumab
pico.intervention: Oral neratinib 240 mg daily for 12 months

arms.label: Neratinib
arms.doseSourceQuote: Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive oral neratinib 240 mg per day or matching placebo.

publications.title: Neratinib after trastuzumab-based adjuvant therapy in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer (ExteNET): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
publications.label: Primary 2-year analysis

publications.title: Neratinib after trastuzumab-based adjuvant therapy in HER2-positive breast cancer (ExteNET): 5-year analysis of a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
publications.label: 5-year analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: At 2 year follow-up, 70 invasive disease-free survival events had occurred in patients in the neratinib group versus 109 events in those in the placebo group (stratified hazard ratio 0·67, 95% CI 0·50-0·91; p=0·0091). The 2-year invasive disease-free survival rate was 93·9% (95% CI 92·4-95·2) in the neratinib group and 91·6% (90·0-93·0) in the placebo group.

After a median follow-up of 5·2 years (IQR 2·1-5·3), patients in the neratinib group had significantly fewer invasive disease-free survival events than those in the placebo group (116 vs 163 events; stratified hazard ratio 0·73, 95% CI 0·57-0·92, p=0·0083). The 5-year invasive disease-free survival was 90·2% (95% CI 88·3-91·8) in the neratinib group and 87·7% (85·7-89·4) in the placebo group.

safety.sourceQuote: The most common grade 3-4 adverse events in patients in the neratinib group were diarrhoea (grade 3, n=561 [40%] and grade 4, n=1 [<1%] vs grade 3, n=23 [2%] in the placebo group)
We recorded serious adverse events in 103 (7%) patients in the neratinib group and 85 (6%) patients in the placebo group.

limitations: High rate of grade 3 diarrhoea without prophylaxis
Patients had not received pertuzumab or T-DM1, limiting relevance to contemporary pathways

clinicalImplications.text: Provides an option for extended adjuvant HER2-directed therapy with neratinib after trastuzumab-based treatment in selected higher-risk patients, requiring proactive diarrhoea management.

tumourBoardPearl.text: If neratinib is used, plan antidiarrhoeal prophylaxis or dose escalation from the start — ExteNET did not mandate prophylaxis and grade 3 diarrhoea was common.
